knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=Genotype matrix (or list of matrices for multiple datasets) containing SNP data, must be complete with no missing values ;; y=Phenotype vector (or list of vectors for multiple datasets), can be continuous or binary ;; clvar=Control variables matrix (or list of matrices), can be omitted or set to NULL if not present ;; block=A data.frame defining the second level of the tree structure (e.g., chromosomes) with columns "colname" and "block" ;; dendr=The hierarchical tree object returned by cluster_var or cluster_position ;; family=Model family, set to "binomial" for binary response (logistic regression) or "gaussian" for continuous response ;; parallel=Parallelization method ("no", "multicore", or "snow") ;; ncpus=Number of cores to use for parallel computing ;; agg.method=Method to aggregate p-values for multiple datasets ("Tippett" or "Stouffer")
- alternatives: hierGWAS=The predecessor package which hierinf re-implements and extends ;; mice, mi, missForest=Packages recommended for missing value imputation before running hierinf ;; PLINK=Tool mentioned for generating the toy dataset ;; Fast linear mixed models (Lippert et al., 2011; Zhou and Stephens, 2014)=Alternative algorithms for pooled GWAS, whereas hierinf advocates meta-analysis/p-value aggregation to handle heterogeneity and improve computation
- when_to_use: Use when performing genome-wide association studies (GWAS) or high-dimensional multivariate linear regression where you want to control the familywise error rate (FWER) while testing groups or regions of highly correlated SNPs at adaptive resolutions.
- pitfalls: Missing values=hierinf requires complete observations (no missing values in the data); missing values must be imputed prior to analysis ;; Input format=Genotype data must be a matrix (or list of matrices), not a data.frame, to ensure fast computation ;; Reproducibility in parallel computing=Must set RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG") and a seed before running parallelized functions to ensure reproducible results ;; List ordering=For multiple datasets, the order of elements in the lists for x, y, and clvar must be identical ;; Operating system limitations=parallel = "multicore" (forking) works on Unix/Mac but not on Windows; use parallel = "snow" on Windows

workflows.name: single_study_hierarchical_inference
workflows.intent: Perform hierarchical testing on a single GWAS dataset using either correlation-based or position-based clustering.
workflows.stages: 1. Define the second level of the tree structure (blocks/chromosomes) ;; 2. Cluster the SNPs using cluster_var (correlation-based) or cluster_position (position-based) ;; 3. Perform hierarchical testing using test_hierarchy ;; 4. Print results and optionally compute R2 for significant clusters using compute_r2
workflows.code:
# Define the second level of the tree structure.
block <- data.frame("colname" = paste0("SNP.", 1:1000),
                    "block" = rep(c("chrom 1", "chrom 2"), each = 500),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Cluster the SNPs
dendr <- cluster_var(x = sim.geno,
                     block = block)

# Store the positions of the SNPs.
position <- data.frame("colnames" = paste0("SNP.", 1:1000),
                       "position" = seq(from = 1, to = 1000),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


# Build the hierarchical tree based on the position
# The argument block defines the second level of the tree structure.
dendr.pos <- cluster_position(position = position,
                              block = block)

# Test the hierarchy using multi sample split
set.seed(1234)
result <- test_hierarchy(x = sim.geno,
                         y = sim.pheno,
                         clvar = sim.clvar,
                         # alternatively: dendr = dendr.pos
                         dendr = dendr,
                         family = "binomial")

print(result, n.terms = 4)

(coln.cluster <- result$res.hierarchy[[2, "significant.cluster"]])

compute_r2(x = sim.geno, y = sim.pheno, clvar = sim.clvar,
           res.test.hierarchy = result, family = "binomial",
           colnames.cluster = coln.cluster)

workflows.name: multiple_studies_meta_analysis
workflows.intent: Jointly analyze multiple GWAS datasets by estimating a single hierarchical tree and aggregating p-values across studies.
workflows.stages: 1. Define the second level of the tree structure (blocks/chromosomes) ;; 2. Cluster the SNPs across datasets using cluster_var or cluster_position ;; 3. Perform hierarchical testing and aggregate p-values using test_hierarchy with an aggregation method ;; 4. Print results
workflows.code:
# The datasets need to be stored in different elements of a list.
# Note that the order has to be the same for all the lists.
# As a simple example, we artificially split the observations of the
# toy dataset in two parts, i.e. two datasets.
set.seed(89)
ind1 <- sample(1:500, 250)
ind2 <- setdiff(1:500, ind1)
sim.geno.2dat  <- list(sim.geno[ind1, ],
                       sim.geno[ind2, ])
sim.clvar.2dat <- list(sim.clvar[ind1, ],
                       sim.clvar[ind2, ])
sim.pheno.2dat <- list(sim.pheno[ind1],
                       sim.pheno[ind2])

# Cluster the SNPs
dendr <- cluster_var(x = sim.geno.2dat,
                     block = block)

# Test the hierarchy using multi sample split
set.seed(1234)
result <- test_hierarchy(x = sim.geno.2dat,
                         y = sim.pheno.2dat,
                         clvar = sim.clvar.2dat,
                         dendr = dendr,
                         family = "binomial")

print(result, n.terms = 4)
